issues.description: Problem statement instructs students to "directly call the public `vector_normalization` and `matrix_normalization` methods" in dd.py, but both template and solution implementations define these helpers as private functions named `__vector_normalization` and `__matrix_normalization` (and do not expose public functions with the names mentioned). This mismatch between the documentation and the actual API/visibility in dd.py may confuse students about which functions they are expected to call and how to normalize DD nodes.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the problem statement to instruct students to use the existing public API (e.g., use make_dd which performs normalization internally) or modify dd.py to provide public wrappers named `vector_normalization` and `matrix_normalization` (which call the existing implementations) so the documented function names actually exist and are callable by students.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to "directly call the public `vector_normalization` and `matrix_normalization` methods" in dd.py, but the actual implementation in dd.py defines these functions with leading double underscores (__vector_normalization and __matrix_normalization). This mismatch names the same conceptual utilities differently across artifacts and may lead students to search for non-existent public identifiers or to misunderstand which API they are expected to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the problem statement to refer to the actual helper names used in dd.py (i.e., __vector_normalization and __matrix_normalization) or expose public functions named vector_normalization and matrix_normalization in dd.py (e.g., add wrapper functions without leading underscores or rename the existing functions) so that the API names are consistent between the instructions and the code.
